_doc: Scenarios run against every template ('all') and per template. 'fox' is deep-merged over the template's defaults to make fox.json. Times are virtual.

all.name: soak-8h
all._doc: a whole hunt of virtual time under the 90 s watchdog: every wait must feed it, nothing may raise, the heap is collected each cycle; keyed_min is set for the slowest template (QRSS)

all.name: module-reset
all._doc: the SA8x8 lost power at 100 s and came back on its default channel; the fox must re-tune before keying again

all.name: module-noreply-then-ok
all._doc: the module was not awake at boot (radio=noreply); once it answers the fox sets it up and tunes it

all.name: play-raises
all._doc: the port refuses a PWM frequency once, mid-song (RuntimeError): logged, PTT released, the next cycle goes on

all.name: recovery-off
all._doc: limits.recover=false: the watchdog stays off and the PWM refusal ends code.py as it did before 1.6

morse-songs.name: body-raises-watchdog-stays
morse-songs._doc: a template body that raises outside tx ends code.py; the watchdog must still be running then, so the board resets after watchdog_s and safemode.py brings it back (foxlib used to disarm it on the way out)
code_patch:
tx.morse(tx.id_message)
    tx.morse(tx.id_message)
    if tx.cycle == 1:
        raise ValueError("a template bug")

wifi-beacon.name: channels-per-wake
wifi-beacon._doc: net.channels: a channel drawn per wake from the list; over 8 wakes at least two different ones

wifi-beacon.name: shell-game-seat-0
wifi-beacon._doc: four identities, 30 s period (validator minimum is 60; the sim uses 60 with 20 s cycles), clock set: the identity advances with the clock

prints_contain: shell game: identity 1 of 3, FOX-A F2:00:00:00:00:0A
shell game: the board clock is unset; keeping seat 1's identity

wifi-beacon.name: sense-tags
wifi-beacon._doc: hunter tags: HUNT- prefix above rssi_min is logged to near.csv; a weak tag and another name are not

wifi-beacon.name: relay-up
wifi-beacon._doc: silent until FOX-2 is heard (from 40 s), then on the air for good

prints_contain: silent this wake (relay: waiting for FOX-2)
relay: on the air from now on

wifi-beacon.name: relay-down
wifi-beacon._doc: silent while FOX-2 is on the air (0-30 s), on the air after

prints_contain: silent this wake (relay: FOX-2 is on the air)

wifi-beacon.name: relay-toggle
wifi-beacon._doc: each return of FOX-2 after an absence flips the fox: heard 0-15 s (off), gone, heard again from 45 s (on)

wifi-beacon.name: crowd-quiet
wifi-beacon._doc: ten advertisers nearby for the first 30 s: more than max 8, so quiet for 60 s, then back

prints_contain: crowd: 10 advertisers above -75 dBm (max 8); quiet for 60 s

wifi-beacon.name: honeypot-probes
wifi-beacon._doc: wifi.Monitor before each wake: a probe for our SSID is logged, one for another network only counted

prints_contain: honeypot: 1 probe(s) for our names, 1 other probe request(s) on ch
honeypot: this build has no wifi.Monitor; probe requests are not logged (joins still are)

wifi-beacon.name: honeypot-listens-on-this-wakes-channel
wifi-beacon._doc: with net.channels the probe listen uses the channel drawn for this wake, not the last one

wifi-beacon.name: safemode-count-cleared
wifi-beacon._doc: a network fox that came back from 3 brownouts says so and clears safemode.py's count after its first wake (else 50 brownouts over its life would strand it in safe mode)

prints_contain: note: 3 safe-mode resets since the last completed wake

wifi-beacon.name: near-log-rate
wifi-beacon._doc: a tag beside the fox for 12 wakes is on the console every wake but written to near.csv once (NEAR_EVERY_S 300)

wifi-beacon.name: mac-set-before-anything-is-sent
wifi-beacon._doc: CircuitPython's mac_address_ap raises unless the AP mode is on; the driver sets it with the radio stopped, so no beacon ever carries the chip's own address

wifi-beacon.name: mac-read-only-build-is-said-once
wifi-beacon._doc: a build whose MAC cannot be set: the fox runs on the chip's address and says so once

prints_contain: note: MAC F2:B0:00:00:00:01 was asked for, the radio reports 7C:DF:A1:00:00:0B (NotImplementedError)

wifi-beacon.name: ap-that-fails-to-start-costs-one-wake
wifi-beacon._doc: start_ap raising once must not end code.py: that wake is silent, the next is on the air

prints_contain: wifi-ap did not start (RuntimeError: AP could not be started); silent this wake

wifi-beacon.name: sense-tag-named-in-the-advertisement
wifi-beacon._doc: a tag whose name is in the advertisement itself (not the scan response) is matched too, once

wifi-beacon.name: ble-workflow-is-switched-off
wifi-beacon._doc: CircuitPython advertises CIRCUITPYxxxx on its own (the BLE workflow; always on builds without native USB such as the ESP32-C3's): the fox switches it off for the run and says so in the banner, and arms the watchdog so a hang resets the board instead of ending the hunt

prints_contain: note: CircuitPython's own BLE advertising (CIRCUITPYxxxx) is off while the fox runs

wifi-beacon.name: trace-the-boot
wifi-beacon._doc: FOX_TRACE in settings.toml: every init step is printed before the banner (with the free heap), so a board that hangs on the way up shows where

wifi-beacon.name: deep-sleep-longer-than-the-watchdog
wifi-beacon._doc: a deep sleep longer than WATCHDOG_S: the timeout covers the sleep plus the jitter and a margin, since a nordic watchdog in RESET mode cannot be stopped and keeps counting through the sleep

wifi-probe.name: probe-list-in-wake
wifi-probe._doc: three networks sought in turn inside one wake: each change is a probe_more in the same burst

wifi-probe.name: probes-for-the-whole-wake
wifi-probe._doc: connect() probes for ~2 s and stops; the runner asks again until the wake is over, so the station is on the air for the wake, under the configured MAC

prints_contain: stealth: BLE only; Wi-Fi radio off
split clue's Wi-Fi half is dropped

ble-beacon.name: checkpoint-service
ble-beacon._doc: the checkpoint service on a BLE fox: connectable, service UUID in the scan response, name shortened

ble-beacon.name: tlm-data
ble-beacon._doc: the TLM frame carries fixed numbers instead of the measured ones

ble-beacon.name: modes-in-turn
ble-beacon._doc: ble on even cycles, an access point on odd ones; the name follows the fox

ble-beacon.name: variable-power-slot-ble
ble-beacon._doc: BLE power re-drawn while advertising: the beacon must stop before it starts again (_bleio refuses a second start)

ble-beacon.name: feature-fails-to-load
ble-beacon._doc: a feature module that cannot be imported on the board (as netpayload.py could not, foxlib 1.4-1.10) is named loudly in the boot log, not as 'not built yet', and the fox still beacons

prints_contain: ** payload failed to load on this board (
prints_not_contain: payload is accepted but not in foxlib

ble-beacon.name: ble-mac-is-the-one-on-the-air
ble-beacon._doc: _bleio.Address is little-endian: the configured MAC must be the advertiser's address, read back the right way round

ble-beacon.name: ble-mac-top-bits-are-set-and-said
ble-beacon._doc: a static random address needs its two top bits: 02:.. goes on the air as C2:.., said once

prints_contain: note: a BLE address has its two top bits set: MAC 02:11:22:33:44:55 is on the air as C2:11:22:33:44:55

ble-beacon.name: nrf-power-step-is-the-nearest
ble-beacon._doc: the nRF SoftDevice refuses a power that is not one of its steps; the fox must advertise at the nearest, not die

prints_contain: note: this chip has no 9 dBm BLE step; advertising at 8 dBm

ble-beacon.name: esp32-refuses-to-advertise-after-a-scan-reset
ble-beacon._doc: XIAO ESP32S3 2026-11-18: after a BLE scan the stack refused start_advertising (error 530) until the adapter was turned off and on; a sense fox scans before every wake, so it must recover and say so once

prints_contain: note: BLE start refused (RuntimeError: Unknown system firmware error: 530); adapter reset and started

ble-beacon.name: esp32-refuses-to-advertise-after-a-scan-restart
ble-beacon._doc: the same refusal cleared by a plain stop and start: said once, no adapter reset

prints_contain: note: BLE start refused (RuntimeError: Unknown system firmware error: 530); started on the second try

ble-beacon.name: esp32-power-value-refused-is-the-callers-error
ble-beacon._doc: on the ESP32 a power the stack refuses is not an nRF step problem: the original error reaches the caller, and the wake is silent, not the fox dead

prints_contain: ble did not start (RuntimeError: Unknown system firmware error: 7); silent this wake

ble-beacon.name: ble-workflow-already-off-is-not-mentioned
ble-beacon._doc: a build with native USB (nRF52840, ESP32-S3 with USB) advertises only after a double-tap reset: nothing to switch off, nothing said

prints_contain: payload: name this cycle "WHO AM I"

checkpoint.name: portal-phone
checkpoint._doc: an iPhone joins: DNS for the captive check, GET hotspot-detect, then the hunter posts a callsign; finds.csv gets the row

prints_contain: checkpoint: portal at http://192.168.4.1/ with captive DNS

checkpoint.name: portal-and-ble-service
checkpoint._doc: the BLE service beside the access point: a central writes a callsign to the characteristic

checkpoint.name: stop-after-finds
checkpoint._doc: the second callsign handed in ends the fox's day: radio down, LED done, no more wakes

prints_contain: done: 2 finds (stop_after_finds); off the air until power-cycled
